Definition: from G4253 and a derivative of G5087; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with G2250 implied) a designated day:--time appointed.
BiblicalUsage: Prothesmios means fixed beforehand, appointed, a set day. It appears once, in Paul's picture of the heir: the heir is under tutors and governors until the time appointed of the father.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Father keeps His own calendar: the heir waits until the appointed day, and the day comes exactly when He set it.
